name: The Corbin family of Heald's company, in the fort
head: corbin_fielding

present_on_scene_date.note: The family's men, women and children are on Helm's and Heald's lists of 1812-1814 (Quaife App. IV, VI).

associated_with.note: No source says which room of the fort any soldier or soldier's family lived in; the barracks named here is the reconstructed choice (liberty L-1812-people-3461).

not_in_this_household.note: A child the counts of 18 do not name may have been of this family; those children have their own reconstructed cards (hh_garrison_children_unnamed_1812).

persons.name: Fielding Corbin

occupation.note: His rank as the muster-roll of the company to 31 May 1812 (Quaife 1913, Appendix VIII) prints it.

present_on_scene_date.note: An account of the battle or of its captives names him, so he was with the garrison when it marched. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: On the muster-roll of the company to 31 May 1812 (Quaife 1913, Appendix VIII), enlisted 25 Oct 1811 for five years, to 25 Oct 1816. After 14 August: One of the nine who reached Plattsburg in May 1814; his pregnant wife was killed in the battle.

persons.name: Mrs. Corbin

present_on_scene_date.note: Helm lists Mrs. Corbin killed in the action. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Wife of Private Fielding Corbin. Kirkland prints a later tradition (Mrs. Callis, daughter of agent Jouett, who arrived c.1817) of 'Sukey Corbin (a camp-follower and washerwoman)' whose children were killed; Kirkland himself says 'perhaps the same Mrs. Corbin' and calls it less authentic. Quaife allows Mrs. Corbin may have had no children. Do not treat 'Sukey' as her established name. After 14 August: Killed in the battle, refusing capture; far advanced in pregnancy (Niles).
